text: When designing a REST API, following a few best practices can make life much easier for developers. First, structure your endpoints around clear resources, using nouns like `/users` or `/orders` instead of verbs. Second, always use standard HTTP status codes—for example, `200` for success, `404` for missing resources, and `400` for bad requests—so clients can understand errors without guessing. Third, version your API from the start, perhaps by adding `/v1/` to the URL path, to avoid breaking existing users when you make changes. Finally, provide thorough documentation that explains each endpoint, its parameters, and sample responses. Good documentation is the bridge between your code and the people who use it.
